question: How do the deployed treasury and contribution primitives adjacent to a cooperative financial pool (Drips, Juicebox and Revnet, Moloch v3 Baal, 0xSplits, Regen Network, Toucan and KlimaDAO, Safe allowance and Zodiac Roles, Hats) work at contract level, at what scale do they run, and what do they fail to do?

frame.population: deployed on-chain treasury, streaming, splitting, role and ecological-credit protocols read from first-party source, contracts, governance records and dated DeFiLlama reads
frame.exposure: contract-level mechanism, admin and upgrade surfaces, deployment addresses, dated scale measurements
frame.comparator: one another, and a cooperative pooling protocol needing treasury, contribution accounting, exit rights and role delegation

item.title: Radicle Drips protocol V2 smart contracts (drips-network/contracts, commit 07c3924)

findings.finding: Drips is a single ERC-20 streaming-and-splitting contract. An account tops up a streams balance and names up to 100 stream receivers; funds leave the streams balance per second but become receivable only at global cycle boundaries of cycleSecs (an immutable set at deployment).
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Every `cycleSecs` seconds the protocol adds streamed funds to the receivers' balances, so recently streamed funds may not be receivable immediately. `cycleSecs` is a constant configured when the Drips contract is deployed.

findings.finding: Received funds are then split: an account sets up to 200 splits receivers with weights summing to 1,000,000; split() pushes each receiver's weight share into that receiver's own splittable balance and the remainder becomes collectable. Anybody may call split for any account, which is how a dependency chain is forced to flow. Splits are non-cycle-gated: they are available immediately and are themselves splittable.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Funds received from splits are available for collection immediately regardless of the cycle. They aren't exempt from being split, so they too can be split when collected. Accounts can build chains and networks of splits between each other. Anybody can request collection of funds for any account, which can be used to enforce the flow of funds in the network of splits.

findings.finding: The split arithmetic is cumulative-weight rounding: receiver i gets floor(amount*cumulativeWeight/1e6) minus what was already assigned, so remainders go to the account itself.
findings.exactSourceLanguage:
uint128 currSplitAmt =
                    uint128(collectableAmt * splitsWeight / _TOTAL_SPLITS_WEIGHT) - splitAmt;

findings.finding: Hard constants: 100 stream receivers per account, 200 splits receivers, 9 extra decimals on amtPerSec, total splits weight 1,000,000, minimum stream rate of 1 token per cycle, per-token protocol balance capped at int128 max.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: uint256 internal constant _MAX_STREAMS_RECEIVERS = 100; ... uint8 internal constant _AMT_PER_SEC_EXTRA_DECIMALS = 9; ... uint256 internal constant _MAX_SPLITS_RECEIVERS = 200; ... uint32 internal constant _TOTAL_SPLITS_WEIGHT = 1_000_000;

findings.finding: Account identity is pluggable through numbered drivers: the high 32 bits of every 256-bit account ID name the controlling driver. AddressDriver (account = Ethereum address), NFTDriver (account = ERC-721 token, holder controls it), ImmutableSplitsDriver (anybody creates a splits configuration nobody can change afterwards, always giving away 100 percent), RepoDriver (account = a GitHub repository), RepoSubAccountDriver, RepoDeadlineDriver, and Giver.
findings.exactSourceLanguage:
Every account ID is a 256-bit integer constructed by concatenating:
    /// `driverId (32 bits) | driverCustomData (224 bits)`.

findings.finding: Repository accounts have no owner until an oracle-signed payload assigns one; funds sent to a GitHub repo wait in the account until its maintainer proves control. The current RepoDriver source still contains the Lit-oracle owner-update path and an updatable oracle address; the deployment file lists a separate 'RepoDriver tasks owner' address.
findings.exactSourceLanguage:
By default the accounts have no owners and they can't be controlled by anybody,
/// use `updateOwnerByLit` to update the owner using signed payload obtained from the oracle.

findings.finding: Control surface: every deployed Drips instance is a Managed proxy with an ERC-1967 admin and a set of pausers; the admin upgrades the logic and can pause. Unmanaged implementations are forever paused with admin 0x00.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: All instances of the contracts have admin address `0x00` and are forever paused.

findings.finding: Anybody can squeeze streams from a sender's published streams history before a cycle ends, so a recipient can access funds mid-cycle by presenting the sender's configuration history.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Only funds streamed before `block.timestamp` can be squeezed.

findings.finding: Only amount-preserving ERC-20s are supported; rebasing, fee-on-transfer or restricted tokens can get stuck or lost.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Tokens which rebase the holders' balances, collect taxes on transfers, or impose any restrictions on holding or transferring tokens are not supported. If you use such tokens in the protocol, they can get stuck or lost.

findings.finding: Deployment files exist for Ethereum (cycle 604800 s), Optimism (cycle 86400 s), Filecoin, Metis and testnets. Ethereum Drips 0xd0Dd053392db676D57317CD4fe96Fc2cCf42D0b4, AddressDriver 0x1455d9bD6B98f95dd8FEB2b3D60ed825fcef0610, NFTDriver 0xcf9c49B0962EDb01Cdaa5326299ba85D72405258, ImmutableSplitsDriver 0x1212975c0642B07F696080ec1916998441c2b774, RepoDriver 0x770023d55D09A9C110694827F1a6B32D5c2b373E, Caller 0x60F25ac5F289Dc7F640f948521d486C964A248e5. Optimism Drips 0xd320F59F109c618b19707ea5C5F068020eA333B3 (RepoDriver 0xe75f56B26857cAe06b455Bfc9481593Ae0FB4257, NFTDriver 0x2F23217A87cAf04ae586eed7a3d689f6C48498dB, LZBridgedGovernor 0x07791819560264627e9c4B1308e546667E83B564).

item.title: Drips documentation (drips-network/docs, docs/pages)

findings.finding: Drip Lists are the dependency-funding surface: a donor creates a list of up to 200 GitHub repositories, Ethereum addresses or other Drip Lists, with percentages, and streams or gives to the list; the list forwards after each settlement period. The docs name the period monthly on Ethereum mainnet and daily on other chains; the Ethereum Drips contract reads cycleSecs 604800 (seven days) and the Optimism contract 86400 (one day). A maintainer who claims a repository states their own dependencies and the share of earnings forwarded to them.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: On Drips, anyone can create a _Drip List_ to flexibly send funds to a list of up to 200 open-source GitHub repositories, Ethereum addresses, or other Drip Lists at a time. As project maintainers come to Drips to claim their funds, they themselves are asked to provide a list of other projects they depend on, and can choose to automatically forward a percentage of their earnings to them.

findings.finding: A list that includes another owner's list trusts that owner not to change it.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: If you choose to include someone else's Drip List on yours, **make sure that you trust the list's owner**, because they may at any point in the future change its recipients.

findings.finding: Drips Wave is a recurring bounty program, not a Drips-contract flow: one week per month, issues scored 100/150/200 points, the reward budget divided by point share, payout in USDC on the Stellar network after a seven-day Compliment window, with KYC required to withdraw. Launched with the Stellar ecosystem in January 2026. Operated by the Public Goods Association (Zug, Switzerland) with discretion to adjust points and withhold rewards.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Drips Wave is currently launching with select partners, starting with the Stellar ecosystem in January 2026. ... At the end of each Wave, we calculate your percentage of all points issued during the Wave, and allocate the reward pool accordingly. ... To withdraw your rewards, you must have a verified identity (**KYC

findings.finding: Wave points act as shares of a fixed per-wave pool; complexity fixes the points per issue (Trivial 100, Medium 150, High 200).
findings.exactSourceLanguage: These points act similar to "shares" in the total Reward Pool for the given Wave. The more points a contributor earns relative to others, the larger their slice of the total rewards.

findings.finding: Drips also hosts retroactive public-goods funding rounds (application, badgeholder voting, payout), available only to select partners.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Drips RPGF is currently only available for select partners.

findings.finding: Security record: Spearbit review (November 2023), Code4rena contest (26 wardens, January 2023), internal and independent reviews, Cantina reviews of BridgedGovernor/Giver, the RepoDriver migration to Gelato, and later drivers, Certora formal verification of parts, Immunefi bounty.

item.title: Bananapus nana-core-v5: Juicebox V5 core contracts (commit cb1f992)

findings.finding: A project is an ERC-721 in JBProjects; its behaviour is a queue of rulesets. A ruleset has duration, weight (tokens minted per unit of base currency), a weightCutPercent applied each cycle when the ruleset re-starts, an approvalHook that gates the next queued ruleset, reservedPercent, cashOutTaxRate, baseCurrency, and permission flags (pausePay, allowOwnerMinting, allowTerminalMigration, ownerMustSendPayouts, holdFees, ...).
findings.exactSourceLanguage: struct JBRulesetConfig { uint48 mustStartAtOrAfter; uint32 duration; uint112 weight; uint32 weightCutPercent; ... } struct JBRulesetMetadata { uint16 reservedPercent; uint16 cashOutTaxRate; uint32 baseCurrency; bool pausePay; bool pauseCreditTransfers; bool allowOwnerMinting; ...

findings.finding: When a ruleset ends the next queued one starts; with an empty queue the same ruleset cycles again, with weight reduced by weightCutPercent. Duration 0 with an empty queue lasts indefinitely and a newly queued ruleset takes effect immediately. A JBDeadline approval hook (1 day, 3 days, 7 days deployed) forces a delay between queuing and effect.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: When a ruleset ends: - If there are rulesets in the queue, the project will move on to the next one. - If the ruleset queue is empty, the current ruleset keeps cycling (_i.e._ re-starting with the same duration).

findings.finding: Funds leave a project in two ways: payouts (up to per-ruleset payout limits, resetting each ruleset, split among JBSplits recipients, callable by anybody unless ownerMustSendPayouts) and a surplus allowance (does not reset). Everything above the payout limits is surplus and backs token cash-outs.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Payout limits reset at the start of each ruleset – projects can use rulesets as a regular cadence for recurring payouts. ... Funds in excess of the payout limits are "surplus funds".

findings.finding: Cash-out is a bonding curve on surplus: reclaim = surplus*x/t * ((1-r) + r*x/t), with r the cashOutTaxRate out of 10,000; r=10,000 reclaims nothing and cashing out the whole supply returns all surplus. Issuance is tokens = amount (in base currency) * weight, minus reservedPercent to the reserved split group.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: return mulDiv(base, (JBConstants.MAX_CASH_OUT_TAX_RATE - cashOutTaxRate) + mulDiv(cashOutTaxRate, cashOutCount, totalSupply), JBConstants.MAX_CASH_OUT_TAX_RATE);

findings.finding: Protocol fee: JBMultiTerminal charges FEE = 25 out of 1000 (2.5 percent) on payouts, surplus-allowance use and cash-outs, paid into fee-beneficiary project ID 1 (hardcoded), which mints the payer's tokens in that project; addresses can be registered feeless in JBFeelessAddresses; held fees can be returned on balance addition.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: uint256 public constant override FEE = 25; // 2.5% ... uint256 internal constant _FEE_BENEFICIARY_PROJECT_ID = 1;

findings.finding: Extensibility is by hooks: data hooks rewrite pay and cash-out accounting, pay hooks, cash-out hooks and split hooks run after; this is how 721 tiers, buyback (Uniswap route versus mint), Revnets and Defifa games are built without changing core.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: useDataHookForPay; useDataHookForCashOut; address dataHook;

findings.finding: V5 is described as a fork of V4 fixing one buyback-hook bug, deployed identically (CREATE2 via Sphinx) on Ethereum, Optimism, Base and Arbitrum. Ethereum V5: JBProjects 0x885f707efa18d2cb12f05a3a8eba6b4b26c8c1d4, JBController 0x27da30646502e2f642be5281322ae8c394f7668a, JBMultiTerminal 0x2db6d704058e552defe415753465df8df0361846, JBRulesets 0x6292281d69c3593fcf6ea074e5797341476ab428, JBDirectory 0x0061e516886a0540f63157f112c0588ee0651dcf, JBTokens 0x4d0edd347fb1fa21589c1e109b3474924be87636, JBSplits 0x7160a322fea44945a6ef9adfd65c322258df3c5e, JBTerminalStore 0xfe33b439ec53748c87dcedacb83f05add5014744, JBPermissions 0x04fd6913d6c32d8c216e153a43c04b1857a7793d; 5.1 set: JBController5_1 0xf3cc99b11bd73a2e3b8815fb85fe0381b29987e1, JBMultiTerminal5_1 0x52869db3d61dde1e391967f2ce5039ad0ecd371c, JBRulesets5_1 0xd4257005ca8d27bbe11f356453b0e4692414b056.

item.title: Bananapus nana-core-v6 README and ADMINISTRATION.md (commit 53914d2)

findings.finding: Juicebox V6 core is in development and deployed (deployment files for Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Arbitrum; project tokens NANA, REV, BAN, CPN, DEFIFA, MARKEE) with a documentation set (ARCHITECTURE, INVARIANTS, ADMINISTRATION, RISKS, AUDIT_INSTRUCTIONS).
findings.exactSourceLanguage: `@bananapus/core-v6` is the base protocol package for Juicebox on EVM chains. It defines projects, rulesets, terminals, permissions, token issuance, cash outs, splits, price feeds, and the accounting that the rest of the V6 ecosystem builds on.

findings.finding: V6 admin surface: Ownable protocol-wide contracts JBDirectory, JBProjects, JBPrices, JBFeelessAddresses; project owner is the project NFT holder; operators via JBPermissions; price feeds append-only; the fee-beneficiary project ID hardcoded; a project creation fee settable by the owner within a hardcoded ceiling of 0.001 ether.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Protocol-wide `Ownable` surfaces exist on `JBDirectory`, `JBProjects`, `JBPrices`, and `JBFeelessAddresses`. ... The project creation fee owner can set in `JBProjects` is bounded by the hardcoded `MAX_CREATION_FEE` (`0.001 ether`).

findings.finding: The workspace states its own recovery limits: immutable infrastructure mistakes require replacement and migration; highest-risk actions are controller migration, terminal migration, token binding, price-feed fallback installation, feeless-list changes, and broad permission grants.

item.title: rev-net/revnet-core-v5: REVDeployer and REVLoans (commit 024d584)

findings.finding: A Revnet is a Juicebox project whose owner is the REVDeployer contract itself: it has no human owner after deployment and runs a fixed schedule of stages set at launch.
findings.exactSourceLanguage:
/// @notice `REVDeployer` deploys, manages, and operates Revnets.
/// @dev Revnets are unowned Juicebox projects which operate autonomously after deployment.

findings.finding: A stage is {startsAtOrAfter, initialIssuance, issuanceCutFrequency (at least 24 hours), issuanceCutPercent, splitPercent to the operator, cashOutTaxRate, autoIssuances}. Issuance per unit of base currency falls on a fixed schedule, so earlier payers receive more tokens per unit; cash-out value is the Juicebox bonding curve on surplus with the stage's tax rate.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: @custom:member issuanceCutFrequency The number of seconds between applied issuance decreases. This should be at least 24 hours. ... @custom:member cashOutTaxRate The factor determining how much each token can cash out from the revnet once cashed out.

findings.finding: Revnets cannot turn cash-outs off completely. A 30-day cash-out delay (CASH_OUT_DELAY = 2,592,000 s) applies only when an existing revnet deploys onto a new network, to prevent arbitrage against a brand-new treasury.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Only applies to existing revnets which are deploying onto a new network. - To prevent liquidity/arbitrage issues which might arise when an existing revnet adds a brand-new treasury. @dev 30 days, in seconds.

findings.finding: The deployer charges a 2.5 percent cash-out fee (FEE = 25 of 1000) when the cash-out tax rate is above zero, paid to the fee revnet; suckers (cross-chain bridges) pay none.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The cash out fee (as a fraction out of `JBConstants.MAX_FEE`). Cashout fees are paid to the revnet with the `FEE_REVNET_ID`. @dev Fees are charged on cashouts if the cash out tax rate is greater than 0%. @dev When suckers withdraw funds, they do not pay cash out fees.

findings.finding: REVLoans lets a holder borrow against tokens: the collateral tokens are burned and reminted on repayment, the borrowable amount equals the cash-out amount, and the loan is an ERC-721. Upfront fee: 2.5 percent to the underlying protocol, 2.5 percent to the issuing revnet, and a borrower-chosen prepaid percent (minimum 2.5, maximum 50) to the fee-receiving revnet that buys a prepaid duration; afterwards repayment costs more, and after 3650 days the collateral cannot be recouped.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Tokens used as collateral are burned, and reminted when the loan is paid off. ... The borrowable amount is the same as the cash out amount. ... After the prepaid duration, the loan will increasingly cost more to pay off. After 10 years, the loan collateral cannot be recouped.

item.title: HausDAO/Baal: Moloch v3 contracts (commit ee3d5ab)

findings.finding: Baal is a Zodiac Module on a Safe avatar: the Safe holds the treasury; Baal executes transfers by module call. Membership is two ERC-20 tokens: Shares (voting weight, BaalVotes delegation with ERC-20 snapshots, Ownable and UUPS-upgradeable) and Loot (economic weight, no vote).
findings.exactSourceLanguage: contract Baal is Module, EIP712Upgradeable, ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable, BaseRelayRecipient { ... (bool success, ) = execAndReturnData(to, amount, "", Enum.Operation.Call);

findings.finding: Proposal lifecycle is Unborn, Submitted, Voting, Grace, Ready, Processed (or Cancelled, Defeated). A proposal is sponsored by anyone holding at least sponsorThreshold shares; non-members may submit with an optional proposalOffering tribute; voting runs votingPeriod seconds, then gracePeriod seconds in which members may exit; processing requires the previous proposal to be finished, so proposals execute in order.
findings.exactSourceLanguage:
/// @return Unborn -> Submitted -> Voting -> Grace -> Ready -> Processed
    ///         \-> Cancelled  \-> Defeated

findings.finding: Passing requires more yes than no votes, quorumPercent of maxTotalSharesAtSponsor in yes votes, and the minRetentionPercent guard: if total shares plus loot has fallen below minRetentionPercent of the high-water mark during the vote (people exited), the proposal auto-fails.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: if (okToExecute && prop.yesVotes * 100 < quorumPercent * prop.maxTotalSharesAtSponsor) okToExecute = false; ... (totalSupply()) < (prop.maxTotalSharesAndLootAtVote * minRetentionPercent) / 100

findings.finding: Ragequit: at any time (not only in the grace period) a member burns shares and/or loot and receives pro-rata (burned/(totalShares+totalLoot)) of each listed token the Safe holds, ETH included; tokens must be passed in ascending address order.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: uint256 amountToRagequit = ((lootToBurn + sharesToBurn) * balance) / _totalSupply; /*calculate 'fair shair' claims*/

item.title: gnosisguild/zodiac-modifier-roles: packages/evm contracts (commit 820e5bc)

findings.finding: Roles is a Safe-interface modifier between modules and the Safe: roles assigned to addresses with assignRoles; each role scopes targets, functions and parameter conditions (allowTarget, scopeTarget, allowFunction, scopeFunction) and whether call, delegatecall or send is allowed; a member calls execTransactionWithRole and the Safe executes only if the call matches the role's permission tree.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Modules that have been granted a role are able to unilaterally make calls to any approved addresses, approved functions, and using approved parameters.

findings.finding: Allowances are keyed budgets with refill: Allowance {refill, maxRefill, period, balance, timestamp}; each period adds refill up to maxRefill; consumption is tracked per allowance key (Consumption {allowanceKey, balance, consumed}) so one budget can be shared across permissions; setAllowance is onlyOwner (the Safe).

item.title: Hats-Protocol/hats-protocol: Hats.sol and HatsIdUtilities.sol (commit cccb71a) with lastTopHatId reads

findings.finding: Hats are non-transferable ERC-1155 role tokens arranged in trees: one top hat per tree, admins at each level (max 14 levels, hat ids pack the path), a hat has a wearer set (max supply), an eligibility module (can the wearer wear it, and are they in good standing) and a toggle module (is the hat active), both either an address or a contract queried on every balanceOf, so a hat is revoked by changing module state with no transaction against the wearer.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Hats Protocol is a protocol for DAO-native roles and credentials that supports revocable delegation of authority and responsibility. Hats are represented on-chain by non-transferable tokens that conform to the ERC1155 interface. An address with a balance of a given Hat token "wears" that hat

findings.finding: Hats.sol contains no owner, proxy or upgrade code (zero matches for Ownable, upgrade, Proxy); hats can be made immutable by their admin (makeHatImmutable); top-hat trees can be linked under another tree with a request and approval pair (requestLinkTopHatToTree, approveLinkTopHatToTree).
